title: Six-year gymnasium selection and effectiveness
title_hu: A hatosztályos gimnáziumi szelekció és eredményesség
outlet: Munkaerőpiaci Tükör 2022 — társadalmi egyenlőtlenség és mobilitás
summary_en: Hungary tracks 10-year-olds into a selective six-year gymnasium track on the basis of an entrance exam. Horn uses OKM and KIR longitudinal data to ask whether the six-year-gymnasium offers a measurable value-added to its students (over and above selection on prior achievement) and how its existence reshapes the rest of the school system. The chapter finds modest positive value-added for selected students alongside substantial negative composition effects on the schools they leave behind.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for the recurring Hungarian debate over track-allocation age (BM Köznevelési Stratégia): the paper provides the empirical case that the six-year-gymnasium track delivers a small individual gain at a meaningful system-level equity cost, which informs proposals to delay entry or restrict the share of pupils admitted. Useful input for the Hungarian national-curriculum review.
